cards.text: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy are writing to the church of the Thessalonians (2 Thessalonians 1:1), and the letter is nearly done. They've just said they're sure the church will keep doing what they command (2 Thessalonians 3:4). Now here comes a command, given in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the church is commanded to keep away from any brother who does what?
Paul reminds the church that when his team was with them, they weren't undisciplined. True or false: back then, his team ate people's food without paying for it.

cards.text: Instead, in labor and toil, they worked NIGHT and DAY. Friend, I need a sit-down after ONE batch.

cards.question: Paul's team worked night and day so they wouldn't be a ___ to any of them.
Paul says his team did have the right to be supported by the believers. So why work night and day anyway?

answers.text: To be an example to imitate
To prove they were the strongest
To save up for the next trip

cards.question: Even while Paul was with them, he gave them a command about work. What was it?

answers.text: Anyone unwilling to work shall not eat
Anyone who works shall rest each week
Anyone who eats shall share with others

cards.question: Paul has heard news. Some of them are leading undisciplined lives. True or false: they're getting a lot accomplished.

cards.text: They're accomplishing nothing but being busybodies. Friend, I spent years tossed in the back of a junk drawer with NO job, and I STILL kept score on every rubber band stretching contest in there.

cards.question: By our Lord Jesus Christ, Paul commands and urges them to begin working ___ to earn their own living.
Then Paul turns to the rest of the brothers. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Don't get tired of doing good

cards.text: As for anyone who won't obey what this letter says, Paul tells the church to take note of him and not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.

cards.question: The church keeps its distance from the person who won't obey the letter. How does Paul say they should see him?
Near the end, Paul writes: may the Lord of peace Himself give them peace. True or false: Paul limits that peace to hard times.

cards.text: Paul adds, "The Lord be with all of you." Then he takes the pen and writes the greeting himself.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says writing the greeting in his own hand is his mark in every letter.

cards.text: And Paul signs off with grace: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you."
